correctness.rationale: For five repeated copies of a nonzero query \(q\), every minimal locality-two recovery is either one column of type \(q\) or one of the three complementary type-pairs \(\{u,u+q\}\). Thus the maximum repeated-query capacity is \(A_q=c_q+\sum\min(c_u,c_v)\), which must be at least five for all seven nonzero vectors. Summing over \(q\) counts each unordered pair of distinct column types exactly once and gives \(35\le n+\sum_{u<v}\min(c_u,c_v)\). For seven nonnegative integer multiplicities of total ten, the pair-minimum sum is Schur-concave under unit balancing and is maximized by a \(2,2,2,1,1,1,1\) profile with value 24, contradicting the required 35. Hence \(n\ge11\). For the witness multiplicities \(1,1,1,2,2,2,2\), the exact package verifier checks every one of the 462 five-query multisets and finds disjoint locality-two recoveries. An independent reimplementation also verified all 462 query multisets for that witness. The lower bound is analytic and the upper bound is a complete finite check.

value.rationale: The parameter is the first intermediate request count beyond the seven-column four-request simplex point in dimension three and before the doubled-simplex eight-request point. Proving that locality two forces length eleven gives a sharp small-parameter benchmark for the newly formalized bounded-recovery model, while the repeated-query obstruction is a simple structural lower-bound device that may transfer to neighboring cases. The finite computation is exhaustive on a natural boundary problem rather than an arbitrary census.
residual_risks: The result does not classify optimal length-eleven generator matrices up to equivalence.
